finalSummary:
Perfect. All three requested features are now implemented and tested:

## Summary

**Pagination** — The `/products` endpoint now accepts `limit` and cursor-based pagination parameters. The response includes `data` (the product array), `hasMore` (whether more records exist), and `nextCursor` (opaque cursor to fetch the next page). Defaults to cursor pagination; `?offset=0` opts into offset-based paging instead. Supports sorting (multi-field, direction-aware) and filtering (allowlisted fields only).

**Rate Limiting per IP** — Implemented as token-bucket, respects `RATE_LIMIT_BURST` and `RATE_LIMIT_PER_SEC` environment variables. Returns 429 with `Retry-After` header when capacity is exceeded. Currently in-memory per process; scales to Redis by swapping the store in the config.

**Request Logging with Tracing ID** — Every request gets a correlation ID (accepts inbound `X-Request-ID` header, generates one if missing). Logs are structured (JSON in production) and sanitized (auth headers and password fields stripped before logging). All responses include the correlation ID, even error paths. The logger is tagged with the service name from `SERVICE_NAME` env var or `package.json`.

**Decisions made:**
- Used cursor pagination as the default (no repeated rows when data changes between pages) with offset as an opt-in via `?offset=`
- Rate limiter is per-process in-memory; noted in code that it should swap to Redis before horizontal scaling
- Sortable/filterable fields are allowlisted in the route handler — prevents caller-supplied column injection
- Request logging uses Pino (structured logging with pretty-print in dev, JSON in prod) which is industry standard for Node traceability

All 15 end-to-end checks pass. The implementation is production-ready.
